analysis.investment_thesis: Supertech EV is a 2022-incorporated micro-cap (INR 54 Cr) in the hyper-competitive EV 2-wheeler and e-rickshaw space with a negligible ROE of 0.47% and no durable track record. This fails every tenet of my philosophy — no history, no moat, glamour sector, sub-par returns on capital.
key_strengths: Promoter holding is healthy at 69.31%, signalling skin in the game
Low reported P/E of 8.21x (though meaningless at 0.47% ROE)
Exposure to a structurally growing EV segment
key_risks: ROE of 0.47% is effectively zero — capital is earning nothing
Brand-new 2022 vintage with no proven unit economics or cycle-tested balance sheet
Brutal EV 2W/e-rickshaw competition from Ola, TVS, Bajaj, Ather and hundreds of unorganised players
red_flags: Sub-1% ROE indicates the business is not generating real economic profit
Tiny INR 54 Cr market cap in a capital-intensive manufacturing business — scale disadvantage
Zero DII holding — no institutional validation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I invest in boring, predictable compounders with decade-long track records, fortress balance sheets and 18-22% ROEs. Supertech EV is the opposite — a 3-year-old micro-cap in one of the most hyped and competitive manufacturing segments in India, earning a ROE of 0.47%. At that return on equity, shareholders would be better off in a savings account. A P/E of 8x means nothing when earnings are this thin; it is optically cheap but fundamentally a statistical artifact on a tiny profit base.

The EV 2-wheeler and e-rickshaw market is being fought over by well-capitalised incumbents (Bajaj, TVS, Hero, Ola) and scores of unorganised players — there is no path I can see for a INR 54 Cr upstart to build durable pricing power, distribution or brand. The 69.31% promoter stake is the only positive, but integrity and stability cannot be judged on a 2022-incorporated entity. I will happily miss this one and wait for proven consumer businesses at reasonable prices. Avoid.
